name: Founding anniversaries of the Bangsamoro’s provinces, cities and municipalities
note: Each date is the day a town legally began: the date its law took effect or its plebiscite ratified it where a source gives one, otherwise the day its law was passed or signed; a city is dated from its charter. `kind` says which. A town may celebrate a different day; where the town’s own reckoning is recorded, it is used (`tradition`). Drawn from the LGU histories (datasets/lgu/histories.json) and the laws themselves on Lawphil.

areas.name: Basilan
areas.basis: Presidential Decree No. 356 created the Province of Basilan, signed 27 December 1973

areas.name: Lanao del Sur
areas.basis: Republic Act No. 2228 divided Lanao into Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur, approved 22 May 1959

areas.name: Tawi-Tawi
areas.basis: Presidential Decree No. 302 created the Province of Tawi-Tawi, signed 11 September 1973

areas.name: Maguindanao del Norte
areas.basis: Republic Act No. 11550 divided Maguindanao; ratified 17 September 2022, the province took effect on 9 January 2023

areas.name: Maguindanao del Sur
areas.basis: Republic Act No. 11550 divided Maguindanao; ratified 17 September 2022, the province took effect on 9 January 2023

areas.name: Cotabato City
areas.basis: Republic Act No. 2364 made Cotabato a chartered city, approved 20 June 1959

units.name: Akbar
units.basis: Akbar was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 193, passed by the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly on 20 December 2005.

units.name: Al-Barka
units.basis: Al-Barka was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 191, passed by the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly on 20 December 2005. Its creation was ratified in a plebiscite held on 22 May 2006, the same day as that for neighbouring Ungkaya Pukan, also carved from Tipo-Tipo.

units.name: Hadji Mohammad Ajul
units.basis: Hadji Mohammad Ajul was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 192, passed by the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly on 20 December 2005 and ratified in a plebiscite on 22 May 2006.

units.name: Hadji Muhtamad
units.basis: Hadji Muhtamad was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 200, passed by the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly on 22 August 2006. The new town's creation was ratified in a plebiscite held on 25 August 2007.

units.name: Lamitan
units.basis: Republic Act No. 9393, approved 15 March 2007 and ratified 18 June 2007, made Lamitan a city; Datu Kalun founded the settlement in 1886

units.name: Lantawan
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 593, signed 2 December 1974

units.name: Maluso
units.basis: Formerly a municipal district, Maluso was made a regular municipality by Presidential Decree No. 356 of 1973, which created the Province of Basilan.

units.name: Sumisip
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 593, signed 2 December 1974

units.name: Tabuan-Lasa
units.basis: The creation was ratified in a plebiscite held on 29 March 2008.

units.name: Tipo-Tipo
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 593, signed 2 December 1974

units.name: Tuburan
units.basis: Tuburan was created as a municipality by Presidential Decree No. 593, signed on 2 December 1974, which divided the Province of Basilan into 10 municipalities.

units.name: Ungkaya Pukan
units.basis: Ungkaya Pukan was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 190, passed by the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly on 20 December 2005 and ratified in a plebiscite on 22 May 2006.

units.name: Amai Manabilang
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 1243, signed 17 November 1977, created it as the Municipality of Bumbaran

units.name: Bacolod-Kalawi
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Balabagan
units.basis: Congress later passed Republic Act No. 5978, approved on 5 July 1969, which created Balabagan by statute from barrios of Malabang and Dianaton, effective from 16 March 1960, with Barrio Banago as the seat.

units.name: Balindong
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Bayang
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Binidayan
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Buadiposo-Buntong
units.basis: Buadiposo-Buntong was created by Presidential Decree No. 1133, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 4 May 1977.

units.name: Bubong
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Butig
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Calanogas
units.basis: Calanogas was created by Presidential Decree No. 1132, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 4 May 1977.

units.name: Ditsaan-Ramain
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Ganassi
units.basis: Garcia on 18 January 1961, converted it into a municipality on the recommendation of the Lanao del Sur Provincial Board.

units.name: Kapai
units.basis: Executive Order No. 77, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 18 July 1967, declared Kapai a regular municipality effective 1 July 1964, after it met the revenue requirement.

units.name: Kapatagan
units.basis: Kapatagan was created by Batas Pambansa Blg. 168, approved on 8 February 1982. The law separated a large group of barangays from Balabagan and made the site of Barangay Kapatagan the seat of government, subject to a plebiscite held on 17 May 1982 alongside the barangay elections.

units.name: Lumba-Bayabao
units.basis: Garcia on 1 June 1961, converted it into a municipality on the recommendation of the Lanao del Sur Provincial Board.

units.name: Lumbaca-Unayan
units.basis: It was created from part of Lumbatan by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 106, signed by Regional Governor Nur Misuari on 22 November 2000. Residents approved its creation in a plebiscite on 27 November 2004.

units.name: Lumbatan
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Lumbayanague
units.basis: Lumbayanague was created by Presidential Decree No. 1091, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 14 February 1977.

units.name: Madalum
units.basis: Executive Order No. 77, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 18 July 1967, declared it a regular municipality effective 1 July 1964, after its revenue had passed the legal threshold for 4 straight fiscal years.

units.name: Madamba
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Maguing
units.basis: Maguing was created on 4 May 1977 by Presidential Decree No. 1134, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos.

units.name: Malabang
units.basis: The town marks its founding on 1 March 1893

units.name: Marantao
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Marawi
units.basis: Commonwealth Act No. 592 made Dansalan (now Marawi) a city on 19 August 1940; it had been a municipality since 1907

units.name: Marogong
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 1131, signed 4 May 1977

units.name: Masiu
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Mulondo
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Pagayawan
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Piagapo
units.basis: Executive Order No. 431, issued on 9 June 1961, divided the municipal district of Saguiaran in two and created the municipal district of Piagapo.

units.name: Picong
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 1135, signed 4 May 1977, created it as the Municipality of Sultan Gumander

units.name: Poona Bayabao
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Pualas
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Saguiaran
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Sultan Dumalondong
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 36, passed by the Regional Legislative Assembly on 19 June 1995

units.name: Tagoloan II
units.basis: Tagoloan was created by Presidential Decree No. 1548, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 11 June 1978, which separated 39 barangays from Kapai to form a new municipality with its seat at Barangay Tagoloan.

units.name: Tamparan
units.basis: It was a municipal district until Executive Order No. 405, issued on 28 September 1960, converted it into a regular municipality.

units.name: Taraka
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Tubaran
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Tugaya
units.basis: Executive Order No. 42 (25 June 1963) declared it a regular municipality, effective 1 July 1962

units.name: Wao
units.basis: Executive Order No. 418, issued on 22 February 1961, converted the municipal district of Wao into a municipality.

units.name: Barira
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 1188, signed 29 August 1977

units.name: Buldon
units.basis: Republic Act No. 3419, approved 18 June 1961

units.name: Datu Blah T. Sinsuat
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 198 (2005), ratified in a plebiscite in 2006; the act on Lawphil leaves its approval date blank

units.name: Datu Odin Sinsuat
units.basis: Datu Odin Sinsuat began as the town of Dinaig, one of the 10 municipalities that President Manuel Roxas organized in Cotabato province through Executive Order No. 82 in 1947.

units.name: Kabuntalan
units.basis: Executive Order No. 82 of 1947 annexed the municipal district of Tumbao to Cotabato, but Executive Order No. 227, signed on 16 June 1949, organized the former districts of Tumbao and Gambar into the Municipality of Tumbao.

units.name: Matanog
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 780, signed 25 August 1975

units.name: Northern Kabuntalan
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 206, ratified in a plebiscite on 30 December 2006

units.name: Parang
units.basis: Under American rule, Polloc became part of the municipal district of Parang in 1917, and President Manuel Roxas organized Parang as a full municipality through Executive Order No. 82 in 1947.

units.name: Sultan Kudarat
units.basis: The town was first known as Nuling, a municipal district that President Manuel Roxas organized into a municipality through Executive Order No. 82 in 1947, joining the districts of Nuling, Gubpangan and Balut.

units.name: Sultan Mastura
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 89 (approved 13 September 1999), ratified 15 March 2003; corporate existence from 28 April 2003

units.name: Talitay
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 52 of 1996 (session begun 22 April 1996), approved in a plebiscite in 1999; the scanned act shows no date

units.name: Upi
units.basis: Upi was a barrio of Dinaig, now Datu Odin Sinsuat, until Republic Act No. 1248, approved on 10 June 1955, made it a separate municipality.

units.name: Ampatuan
units.basis: Ampatuan was created as a municipality of the old province of Cotabato by Republic Act No. 2509, approved in 1959, which separated 23 barrios from Datu Piang and set the seat of government at Decalungan.

units.name: Buluan
units.basis: Buluan was one of 10 municipalities organized in the old province of Cotabato by Executive Order No. 82 of President Manuel Roxas in 1947, formed from the municipal districts of Buluan and Liguasan around Lake Buluan.

units.name: Datu Abdullah Sangki
units.basis: It was carved out of its mother town, Ampatuan, and its creation was ratified in a plebiscite on 3 January 2004.

units.name: Datu Anggal Midtimbang
units.basis: Voters ratified its creation in a plebiscite on 30 December 2006, and the law set its administrative centre at barangay Brar.

units.name: Datu Hoffer Ampatuan
units.basis: It was formed from 9 barangays of Shariff Aguak and parts of 2 barangays of Datu Unsay, and its creation was ratified in a plebiscite on 30 July 2009, the same day the neighbouring towns of Shariff Saydona Mustapha and Datu Salibo were ratified.

units.name: Datu Paglas
units.basis: Datu Paglas was created on 22 November 1973 by Presidential Decree No. 340 of President Ferdinand Marcos, issued on the day the old province of Cotabato was divided.

units.name: Datu Piang
units.basis: It was organized as the municipality of Dulawan by Executive Order No. 66 of President Manuel L.

units.name: Datu Salibo
units.basis: Its creation was ratified in a plebiscite held by the Commission on Elections on 30 July 2009.

units.name: Datu Saudi-Ampatuan
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 151, passed 14 May 2003 and approved 9 June 2003

units.name: Datu Unsay
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 150, passed 14 May 2003 and approved 9 June 2003

units.name: Gen. S. K. Pendatun
units.basis: It was created on 7 April 1991 by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 3, which carved it out of Buluan.

units.name: Guindulungan
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 139, passed 10 March 2003

units.name: Mamasapano
units.basis: It became a municipality under Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 54, with 18 barangays taken from Shariff Aguak, after a plebiscite on 31 October 1998.

units.name: Mangudadatu
units.basis: It was formed from 8 barangays in the southern part of Buluan, and its creation was ratified in a plebiscite on 30 December 2006, the same day as the neighbouring town of Pandag, which was also carved from Buluan.

units.name: Pagagawan
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 95, passed 18 January 2000

units.name: Pagalungan
units.basis: Pagalungan became a municipality in 1947 under Executive Order No. 82 of President Manuel Roxas, which organized 10 new municipalities in the old province of Cotabato.

units.name: Paglat
units.basis: Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 112, passed 19 July 2001

units.name: Pandag
units.basis: It was formed from 8 barangays in the northern part of Buluan, and its creation was ratified in a plebiscite on 30 December 2006, the same day as Mangudadatu, which was carved from Buluan's southern barangays.

units.name: Rajah Buayan
units.basis: The modern municipality was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 166 of October 2002 and ratified in a plebiscite on 4 September 2004.

units.name: Shariff Aguak
units.basis: Shariff Aguak was founded as Maganoy by Executive Order No. 47 of President Diosdado Macapagal in 1963, which formed the new town from 28 barrios of Datu Piang in the old province of Cotabato.

units.name: Shariff Saydona Mustapha
units.basis: It was created by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 225, as amended by Act No. 252, from barangays of Shariff Aguak, Mamasapano, Datu Unsay, Datu Piang and Datu Saudi-Ampatuan, and was ratified in a plebiscite on 30 July 2009.

units.name: South Upi
units.basis: South Upi was created on 22 September 1976 by Presidential Decree No. 1011 of President Ferdinand Marcos.

units.name: Sultan sa Barongis
units.basis: Sultan sa Barongis was created as the municipality of Lambayong by Executive Order No. 543 of President Elpidio Quirino in October 1952, formed from places in and around the barrios of Barurao and Lambayong in the municipality of Dulawan, now Datu Piang.

units.name: Talayan
units.basis: Presidential Decree No. 1009, signed 22 September 1976

units.name: Kadayangan
units.basis: Kadayangan was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 42, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 7 barangays that had belonged to Midsayap, North Cotabato, and voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Central Labas, Kapinpilan, Malingao, Mudseng, Sambulawan, Tugal and Tumbras.

units.name: Kapalawan
units.basis: Kapalawan was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 45, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 7 barangays that had belonged to Carmen, North Cotabato, and voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Kibayao, Kitulaan, Langogan, Manarapan, Nasapian, Pebpoloan and Tupig.

units.name: Ligawasan
units.basis: Ligawasan was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 48, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 7 barangays that had belonged to Pikit, North Cotabato, and voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Bagoinged, Barungis, Buliok, Bulol, Gli-Gli, Kabasalan and Rajamuda.

units.name: Malidegao
units.basis: Malidegao was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 46, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 7 barangays that had belonged to Pikit, North Cotabato, and voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Balungis, Batulawan, Fort Pikit, Gokotan, Nabundas, Nalapaan and Nunguan.

units.name: Nabalawag
units.basis: Nabalawag was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 43, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 7 barangays that voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Damatulan, Kadigasan, Kadingilan, Kudarangan, Nabalawag and Olandang from Midsayap, and Dungguan from Aleosan, both in North Cotabato.

units.name: Old Kaabakan
units.basis: Old Kaabakan was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 44, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 7 barangays that had belonged to Kabacan, North Cotabato, and voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Buluan, Nangaan, Pedtad, Sanggadong, Simbuhay, Simone and Tamped.

units.name: Pahamuddin
units.basis: Pahamuddin was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 41, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 12 barangays that had belonged to Pigcawayan, North Cotabato, and voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: Balacayon, Buricain, Datu Binasing, Datu Mantil, Kadingilan, Libungan Torreta, Lower Baquer, Lower Pangangkalan, Matilac, Patot, Simsiman and Upper Pangangkalan.

units.name: Tugunan
units.basis: Tugunan was created by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 47, which the Bangsamoro Parliament passed on 17 August 2023. It joins 9 barangays that voted to join the Bangsamoro region in the 2019 plebiscite: 8 from Pikit, among them Balong, Bualan, Lagunde, Macasendeg, Manaulanan, Pamalian and Panicupan, and Tapodoc from Aleosan, both in North Cotabato.

units.name: Bongao
units.basis: Executive Order No. 355, effective 1 July 1958

units.name: Languyan
units.basis: Languyan was created by Presidential Decree No. 1086 on 4 February 1977.

units.name: Mapun
units.basis: Executive Order No. 355 made Cagayan de Sulu a municipality, effective 1 July 1958

units.name: Panglima Sugala
units.basis: Executive Order No. 355 made the district of Balimbing a municipality, effective 1 July 1958

units.name: Sapa-Sapa
units.basis: Sapa-Sapa was created by Presidential Decree No. 1087 on 4 February 1977.

units.name: Sibutu
units.basis: The municipality was created out of Sitangkai by Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 197, ratified in a plebiscite on 21 October 2006, which moved 16 Sitangkai barangays on Sibutu Island to the new town.

units.basis: Executive Order No. 355, effective 1 July 1958

units.basis: Executive Order No. 355, effective 1 July 1958

units.basis: Executive Order No. 355 (26 August 1959), effective 1 July 1958
